annotations.title: His own cross.
annotations.text: This cross, for that it was the instrument of our redemption, and as it were the altar of the supreme sacrifice, highly sanctified by the touching, bearing, and oblation of the sacred body and blood of our Lord, is truly called the Holy Cross: ◦ and hath been endued with virtue of miracles, both the whole and every little piece thereof. For the which causes, and specially for the most need memorial of Christ's Passion, it hath been visited in Pilgrimages, honoured by festival days and otherwise, reserved & reverenced of the ancient fathers, with all devotion: as contrarywise it hath been abused of Pagans, Apostatæs, and Heretics, seeking in vain to deface and destroy it. See S. Cyril li. 6 cont. Iulian. S. Hierom ep. 17. S. Paulinus ep. 11. Ruffinus li. 1. c. 7. & 8. Evagr. histo. li. 4 c. 25. S. Leo ep. 72. and Ser. 8 de Passione. Paulus Diac. li. 18.

annotations.title: To his mother.
annotations.text: <mn>◦</mn> The maruelous respect that Christ had to his mother, vouchsauing to speake to her, and to take order for her euen from the crosse in the middes of his infinite anguishes and mysteries a working for mankind.

notes.text: By this you see why in Catholike Churches MARIE and Iohn stand by the Roode.

annotations.title: To the Disciple.
annotations.text: A great honour to Iohn and charge, to haue that blessed iewel in keeping: and an vnspeakable comfort, that from that day forward the one was to the other mother and sonne. virginem virgini commendauit, saith S. Hierom. He commended the virgin to a virgin. ◦

annotations.title: Bloud and water.
annotations.text: This pearsing of Christs side, though on the souldiars part it was done blindly and insolently, [1] yet by Gods ordinance it conteined great mysteries, and was prefigured by Moyses striking the rocke with his rodde: [2] as this streame of bloud and water drawen miraculously out of his dead body, running in the Sacraments of the Church after the people of God, was signified by the water of the same rocke folowing the Israelites in the desert. Out of this side (saith S. Augustine) [3] issued the Sacraments. Hence (saith S. Chrysostom) [4] the great mysteries haue their beginning. Who warneth vs, that when we come to drinke of the holy chalice, we should so approche, as though we drew the bloud out of Christes side. And both bloud and water apart did flow forth, to shew vs the fountaine of the two principal Sacraments, and their seueral matters, Baptisme and the Eucharist, springing to life euerlasting in the Church. [5] The fathers also say that the Church who is Christs spouse and his coadiutrice in applying the bloud and water to the benefite of the Faithful, was here formed, builded, and taken out of this holy side of Christ sleeping on the Crosse, as [6] Eue was of Adams side, when he was cast a sleepe in Paradise.

notes.text: The Sacraments issued out of Christs side, and thence haue their vertue.
The CHVRCH builded of Christs side, as Eue of Adams.
